method.inputs: Only independently passed evidence records and their exact approved captured-frame hashes. Source URLs and coordinates are checked against saved official source catalogs. Carried-forward non-Busan sources retain their exact, hash-bound baseline metadata; no fresh survey is claimed.
method.canonicalMediaUrl: Lowercase scheme/host, drop default port, decode unreserved path characters, ignore query and fragment for stable-endpoint identity. Common informational source-page URLs are not treated as video duplicates.
method.pHash: 63-bit median threshold of 8x8 low-frequency DCT coefficients, excluding DC, from 32x32 grayscale.
method.perceptualCandidateThreshold: (pHash<=10 AND dHash<=12) OR pHash<=6 OR dHash<=4 across any cross-camera frame pair. These are review candidates only.
method.exactComparison: Recorded uncompressed pixel SHA256 plus independently decoded JPEG RGB SHA256 and JPEG-file SHA256; distinct camera IDs required.
method.coordinates: Exact coordinate coincidences are flagged for review, not automatically considered duplicates; separate cameras can share a pole or landmark.

review.reason: The published resort coordinates are shared. Camera04 shows the mountain slope, foreground trees and snowmaking; camera07 shows a separately framed illuminated Waterplanet facility/open area. All eight captures show distinct fixed scenes; original coordinates are preserved.

Both share the published Sinan intersection coordinates, preserved unchanged. Camera3070 looks diagonally across the curving junction and its foreground traffic island; camera3074 looks lengthwise down the approaching street with a different crosswalk, pole arrangement and lane geometry. All four real captures per source reviewed independently; traffic positions change in each connection.

nearestCameraPairs.purpose: Nearest-pair diagnostic review; not necessarily within similarity threshold.

review.reason: Upper scene is a divided road passing under an overbridge; lower scene is a long bridge over water with a merging side ramp and different rail geometry. All four captures per camera reviewed.

nearestCameraPairs.purpose: Nearest-pair diagnostic review; not necessarily within similarity threshold.

review.reason: Busan212 shows separated bridge decks crossing open water, with long continuous bridge barriers and dense traffic. Gimpo011 shows a broad surface boulevard bordered by apartment blocks, trees, sidewalks and a near street junction. The fixed terrain and road geometry differ in every capture; the day/night difference alone was not used.

nearestCameraPairs.purpose: Nearest-pair diagnostic review; not necessarily within similarity threshold.

review.reason: Both are published viewpoints at Gae-yang junction, facing different approach roads. Camera1200 has green guides sweeping toward the foreground and a narrow right traffic island; camera1204 looks across horizontal foreground lanes with a pink edge line and a different crosswalk and pole arrangement. Fixed road geometry and traffic positions differ in all four captures per source; these are separate camera viewpoints at one junction, not different junctions.

nearestCameraPairs.purpose: Nearest-pair diagnostic review; not necessarily within similarity threshold.

review.reason: Jinju2180 is a close view of a signalized street approach with a yellow hatched island, foreground turning vehicles and a near crosswalk. Sejong1005 is an elevated long view down a wider tree-lined boulevard with a blue-marked lane and a distant junction. Their fixed layout and field of view differ. The day/night difference alone was not used as evidence.

nearestCameraPairs.purpose: Nearest-pair diagnostic review; not necessarily within similarity threshold.

review.reason: Root directly inspected all eight original approved captures, four per camera. The upper scene is a broad junction viewed across horizontal green guide lanes, with a zebra crossing, buses and a queue facing the camera. The lower scene is a much closer oblique approach with a yellow hatched median, differently oriented white dashed lane lines and different roadside geometry. Moving vehicles differ in all observed pairs. The two exact official camera IDs, distinct media paths and separately reported coordinates support the visibly different scenes; geographic metadata alone was not used as the verdict.

limitations: Perceptual hashes are a bounded similarity screen, not a mathematical proof of distinct cameras. Similar road/tunnel geometry needs direct contact-sheet review.
KBS embeds lack exported decoded pixel captures: official cctvId uniqueness and prior operator scene review are verified, but automated KBS cross-camera/cross-provider visual matching is unavailable.
The saved public catalog establishes provider IDs and reported coordinates, not a physical site survey.
